title: source
intro: Time series, with possible error bars and formatting information.

sections.name: arithmetic
sections.desc:
Read a daisy log, weather or data file. Calculate a single value for each time step,
based on the value in the various columns.
sections.sig:
< arithmetic (expr expr )
                    (file file )
                    (with with )
                    (timestep h)
                    (missing missing ...)            ; Has default value.
                    (filter)
                    (original original ...)
                    (dim line dim line )
                    (style style )
                    (title title )
                    (accumulate false)
                    (handle normal)
                    (default hour 8)
                    (time offset time offset ) ; Has default value.
                    (valid valid )                   ; Default true value. >

attrs.name: expr
attrs.doc:
Expression for calculating the value for this source for each row. The expres-
     sion can refer to the value in a specific column by the tag for that column.

attrs.name: file
attrs.doc: Name of Daisy file where data is found.

attrs.name: with
attrs.doc:
Specify style used for the data series on the graph. use ’points’ to plot each
     point individually, or ’lines’ to draw lines between them.
     By default, data from dwf and dlf files will be drawn with lines, and data from
     ddf files will be drawn with points.

attrs.name: timestep
attrs.doc: Multiple with this dimension when accumulating.

attrs.name: missing
attrs.doc:
(missing "" "00.00")
        Parameter description:
        List of strings indicating missing values.

attrs.name: filter
attrs.doc:
Only include data from rows that passes all these filters.
           <   tag allowed ...       >
           – tag: string (see section 4.1.5)
             Parameter
             Name of column in Daisy log file to filter for.
           – allowed : string (see section 4.1.5) sequence
             Parameter
             List of allowable values in filter.

attrs.name: original
attrs.doc:
List of dimensions of the data in the data file.
        If the list has only one element, that element is used as the dimension for
        all columns in the file. Otherwise, the list must have one element for each
        column.
        By default Daisy will use the names specified in data file.

attrs.name: dim line
attrs.doc:
If true, assume the line after the tags contain dimensions. By default this will
        be true iff ’original’ is not specified.

attrs.name: style
attrs.doc:
Style to use for this dataset.
        By default, gnuplot will use style 1 for the first source to plot with lines, style
        2 for the second, and so forth until it runs out of styles and has to start over.
        Points work similar, but with its own style counter. For color plots, points
        and lines with the same style number also have the same color.
        Set style to 0 to reuse the style of the previous series, or to a negative number
        to explicitly request the default behaviour.
        The ’style’ parameter is only used if ’with’ is either ’points’ or ’lines’.

attrs.name: title
attrs.doc:
Name of data series for the legend on the graph.
        By default the name of the ’expr’ object.

attrs.name: accumulate
attrs.doc: Accumulate values.

attrs.name: handle
attrs.doc:
Determine how to handle multiple simultaniously. Possible values are:
     all: show all values.
     sum: use the sum of the values.
     normal: use the arithmetic average of the values, and calculate the standard
     deviation.

attrs.name: default hour
attrs.doc: Hour to assume when nothing else is specified;

attrs.name: time offset
attrs.doc: Add this to time from sources. By default, use unmodified times.

attrs.name: valid
attrs.doc: Ignore entries if this boolean expression is false.

sections.text:
Read a daisy log, weather or data file. Calculate a single value for each time step,
based on the value in the various columns.
  < arithmetic (expr expr )
                    (file file )
                    (with with )
                    (timestep h)
                    (missing missing ...)            ; Has default value.
                    (filter)
                    (original original ...)
                    (dim line dim line )
                    (style style )
                    (title title )
                    (accumulate false)
                    (handle normal)
                    (default hour 8)
                    (time offset time offset ) ; Has default value.
                    (valid valid )                   ; Default true value. >
    expr : number component (see chapter 59)
     Expression for calculating the value for this source for each row. The expres-
     sion can refer to the value in a specific column by the tag for that column.
    file: string (see section 4.1.5)
     Parameter
     Name of Daisy file where data is found.
    with: string (see section 4.1.5)
     Optional parameter
     Specify style used for the data series on the graph. use ’points’ to plot each
     point individually, or ’lines’ to draw lines between them.
     By default, data from dwf and dlf files will be drawn with lines, and data from
     ddf files will be drawn with points.
    timestep: string (see section 4.1.5)
     Parameter (default ‘h’)
     Multiple with this dimension when accumulating.

       missing: string (see section 4.1.5) sequence
        Parameter (has default value with length 2)

        (missing "" "00.00")

        Parameter description:
        List of strings indicating missing values.

       filter : submodel (see section 4.1.7) sequence
        Submodel (default: an empty sequence)
        Only include data from rows that passes all these filters.
           <   tag allowed ...       >

           – tag: string (see section 4.1.5)
             Parameter
             Name of column in Daisy log file to filter for.
           – allowed : string (see section 4.1.5) sequence
             Parameter
             List of allowable values in filter.

       original : string (see section 4.1.5) sequence
        Optional parameter
        List of dimensions of the data in the data file.
        If the list has only one element, that element is used as the dimension for
        all columns in the file. Otherwise, the list must have one element for each
        column.
        By default Daisy will use the names specified in data file.

       dim line: boolean (see section 4.1.2)
        Optional parameter
        If true, assume the line after the tags contain dimensions. By default this will
        be true iff ’original’ is not specified.

       style: integer
        Optional parameter
        Style to use for this dataset.
        By default, gnuplot will use style 1 for the first source to plot with lines, style
        2 for the second, and so forth until it runs out of styles and has to start over.
        Points work similar, but with its own style counter. For color plots, points
        and lines with the same style number also have the same color.
        Set style to 0 to reuse the style of the previous series, or to a negative number
        to explicitly request the default behaviour.
        The ’style’ parameter is only used if ’with’ is either ’points’ or ’lines’.

       title: string (see section 4.1.5)
        Optional parameter
        Name of data series for the legend on the graph.
        By default the name of the ’expr’ object.

       accumulate: boolean (see section 4.1.2)
        Parameter (default false)
        Accumulate values.

    handle: string (see section 4.1.5)
     Parameter (default ‘normal’)
     Determine how to handle multiple simultaniously. Possible values are:
     all: show all values.
     sum: use the sum of the values.
     normal: use the arithmetic average of the values, and calculate the standard
     deviation.

    default hour : integer
     Parameter (default 8)
     Hour to assume when nothing else is specified;

    time offset: Timestep fixed component (see section 107.25)
     Submodel (has fully specified default value)
     Add this to time from sources. By default, use unmodified times.

    valid : boolean component (see chapter 21)
     Component (default ‘true’)
     Ignore entries if this boolean expression is false.

sections.name: combine
sections.desc: Combine data from multiple sources with a single expression.
sections.sig:
< combine (expr expr )
               (source source ...)
               (with with )
               (style style )
               (title title )
               (accumulate false) >

attrs.name: expr
attrs.doc:
Expression for calculating the value for this source for each row. A row is any
     date found in any of the member of ’source’. The expression may refer to the
     value of each source by its title.

attrs.name: source
attrs.doc:
List of sources for data. The style information for the sources is ignored,
        but the dates, title and value is used as specified by ’expr’ to calculate the
        combines date and value pairs.

attrs.name: with
attrs.doc:
Specify style used for the data series on the graph. use ’points’ to plot each
        point individually, or ’lines’ to draw lines between them.
        By default, let the first source decide.

attrs.name: style
attrs.doc:
Style to use for this dataset.
        By default, gnuplot will use style 1 for the first source to plot with lines, style
        2 for the second, and so forth until it runs out of styles and has to start over.
        Points work similar, but with its own style counter. For color plots, points
        and lines with the same style number also have the same color.
        Set style to 0 to reuse the style of the previous series, or to a negative number
        to explicitly request the default behaviour.
        The ’style’ parameter is only used if ’with’ is either ’points’ or ’lines’.

attrs.name: title
attrs.doc:
Name of data series for the legend on the graph.
        By default the name of the ’expr’ object.

attrs.name: accumulate
attrs.doc: Accumulate values.

sections.text:

  < combine (expr expr )
               (source source ...)
               (with with )
               (style style )
               (title title )
               (accumulate false) >

    expr : number component (see chapter 59)
     Expression for calculating the value for this source for each row. A row is any
     date found in any of the member of ’source’. The expression may refer to the
     value of each source by its title.

       source: source component (see chapter 83) sequence
        List of sources for data. The style information for the sources is ignored,
        but the dates, title and value is used as specified by ’expr’ to calculate the
        combines date and value pairs.

       with: string (see section 4.1.5)
        Optional parameter
        Specify style used for the data series on the graph. use ’points’ to plot each
        point individually, or ’lines’ to draw lines between them.
        By default, let the first source decide.

       style: integer
        Optional parameter
        Style to use for this dataset.
        By default, gnuplot will use style 1 for the first source to plot with lines, style
        2 for the second, and so forth until it runs out of styles and has to start over.
        Points work similar, but with its own style counter. For color plots, points
        and lines with the same style number also have the same color.
        Set style to 0 to reuse the style of the previous series, or to a negative number
        to explicitly request the default behaviour.
        The ’style’ parameter is only used if ’with’ is either ’points’ or ’lines’.

       title: string (see section 4.1.5)
        Optional parameter
        Name of data series for the legend on the graph.
        By default the name of the ’expr’ object.

       accumulate: boolean (see section 4.1.2)
        Parameter (default false)
        Accumulate values.

sections.name: merge
sections.desc:
Merge multiple timeseries into one. Any errorbars on the original timeseries are
ignored, but the merged timeseries may have errorbars if there are multiple values
for the same time.
sections.sig:
< merge (source source ...)
              (with with )
              (dimension dimension )
              (style style )
              (title title )
              (accumulate false) >

attrs.name: source
attrs.doc: List of timeseries to merge.

attrs.name: with
attrs.doc:
Specify style used for the data series on the graph. use ’points’ to plot each
        point individually, or ’lines’ to draw lines between them.
        By default, let the first source decide.

attrs.name: dimension
attrs.doc:
Dimension of data to plot. By default use the first source with a known
    dimension.

attrs.name: style
attrs.doc:
Style to use for this dataset.
    By default, gnuplot will use style 1 for the first source to plot with lines, style
    2 for the second, and so forth until it runs out of styles and has to start over.
    Points work similar, but with its own style counter. For color plots, points
    and lines with the same style number also have the same color.
    Set style to 0 to reuse the style of the previous series, or to a negative number
    to explicitly request the default behaviour.
    The ’style’ parameter is only used if ’with’ is either ’points’ or ’lines’.

attrs.name: title
attrs.doc: Name of data series for the legend on the graph.

attrs.name: accumulate
attrs.doc: Accumulate values.
